title: Security Impact of Ascon Zero-Sum Distinguishers
summary: A 12-round Ascon zero-sum distinguisher falls below the claimed work threshold but has very small advantage; its impact on Ascon AEAD or Hash security remains unresolved.

formal_statement.body: A low-complexity zero-sum distinguisher for the 12-round Ascon permutation requires less work than Ascon's claimed security level, but its distinguishing advantage over a perfect permutation is very small, typically less than a factor of $2$. Determine whether this non-ideal property of the permutation yields any concrete security implication for the Ascon AEAD or Hash modes, or establish that it does not affect their security.

scope.domain: Structural cryptanalysis of the 12-round Ascon permutation via a zero-sum distinguisher, with possible consequences for its AEAD and Hash modes.
parameters: 12 rounds — number of Ascon permutation rounds targeted by the distinguisher
Ascon's claimed security level — comparison point for the distinguisher's work
Factor of 2 — typical scale stated for the small distinguishing advantage over a perfect permutation
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine whether the permutation's non-ideal zero-sum property has any concrete security implication for Ascon AEAD or Hash, or establish that it does not affect their security.

citations.label: Revisiting Higher-Order Differential-Linear Attacks from an Algebraic Perspective

progress.summary: The source reports a 12-round Ascon zero-sum distinguisher requiring less work than the claimed security level while offering only a very small advantage over a perfect permutation. It leaves any impact on Ascon AEAD and Hash unclear while judging such an impact very likely nonexistent.
citation_labels: Kai Hu et al., Revisiting Higher-Order Differential-Linear Attacks from an Algebraic Perspective
